answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a garden: newcomers arrive as seedlings with near-zero trust and must grow a slow, public record of verified work before earning rewards. A trellis gives that growth structure, because each contribution is tied to earlier ones, so one operator cannot spin up dozens of disconnected identities without the pattern showing. Peers take the pulse of the garden on a regular rhythm, checking whether work is real and varied; clusters that move in lockstep are paused for review. Standing is earned gradually and cannot be bought or cloned.
